Almost everything on this blog comes from courses, books and papers that their authors chose to share. I have met almost none of the people below, yet I learn from their work every week. Thank you: to the instructors and authors named here, and to the teaching assistants, course staff and video teams whose names are often not on the page but who made these materials usable.

## Courses and lectures

### SLAM and state estimation

- **Cyrill Stachniss** (University of Bonn): [graph-based SLAM lectures](https://www.ipb.uni-bonn.de/online-training-robotics/)
- **Luca Carlone** (MIT): [16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/16-485-visual-navigation-for-autonomous-vehicles-vnav-fall-2020/)
- **Daniel Cremers** (TU Munich): [Multiple View Geometry](https://cvg.cit.tum.de/_media/teaching/ss2025/mvg/multiviewgeometry8.pdf)
- **The MUDE team** (TU Delft): [Observation Theory](https://mude.citg.tudelft.nl/book/2025/observation_theory/01_Introduction.html)

## Books

- **Timothy D. Barfoot**: [*State Estimation for Robotics*](https://asrl.utias.utoronto.ca/~tdb/), 2nd edition
- **Luca Carlone, Ayoung Kim, Timothy Barfoot, Daniel Cremers and Frank Dellaert**, editors, and all the chapter authors: [*The SLAM Handbook*](https://asrl.utias.utoronto.ca/~tdb/slam/)
- **Frank Dellaert and Michael Kaess**: *Factor Graphs for Robot Perception*
- **Nicolas Boumal**: [*An Introduction to Optimization on Smooth Manifolds*](https://www.nicolasboumal.net/book)
- **Peter Teunissen**: *Testing Theory: An Introduction*

## Papers, surveys and tutorials

- **Surveys and tutorials:** Tosi et al., *How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM* (2024); Grisetti et al., *A Tutorial on Graph-Based SLAM* (2010); Solà et al., *A micro Lie theory for state estimation in robotics* (2018); Schubert et al., [*Visual Place Recognition: A Tutorial*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03281) (2023)
- **Rendering and Gaussians:** Zwicker et al., *EWA Splatting* (2002); Mildenhall et al., *NeRF* (2020); Kerbl et al., *3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering* (2023); Ye and Kanazawa, *Mathematical Supplement for the gsplat Library* (2023); Yu et al., *Mip-Splatting* (2024); Huang et al., *2D Gaussian Splatting* (2024)
- **Dense and Gaussian SLAM:** Newcombe et al., *KinectFusion* (2011); Keetha et al., *SplaTAM* (2024); Matsuki et al., *Gaussian Splatting SLAM* (2024); Huang et al., *Photo-SLAM* (2024); Zhu et al., *LoopSplat* (2025)
- **Optimization and robustness:** Yang et al., *Graduated Non-Convexity for Robust Spatial Perception* (2020); Mangelson et al., *Pairwise Consistent Measurement Set Maximization for Robust Multi-robot Map Merging* (2018); Teed and Deng, *DROID-SLAM* (2021); Murai et al., *MASt3R-SLAM* (2025)
- **Learned 3D priors:** Wang et al., *DUSt3R* (2024); Wang et al., *VGGT* (2025)

Thank you as well to MIT OpenCourseWare and to every university and lab above that publishes its teaching openly, to the people who maintain the open-source tools these posts are built with (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, gsplat, GTSAM, Open3D and Quarto among them), and to the teachers I have learned from in person.

Course materials, books and papers belong to their authors. When a post uses a figure, an equation or a result from one of them, it credits the source where it appears. If I have credited someone wrongly or left someone out, please [open an issue](https://github.com/zerokhong1/blog/issues).
